record.question: Which type of necrosis is typically seen in the brain following an ischemic event (stroke)?
record.explanation: Answer D: Liquefactive necrosis. Cerebral infarction after ischemia typically evolves to liquefactive necrosis; ischemia in most other organs more often produces coagulative necrosis. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430935/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557627/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
